_meta.description: Government of India agricultural schemes, used to ground the advisory chatbot. Figures current as of the 2024-25 cycle; always verify against the official portal before advising a farmer.
_meta.source_note: Compiled from Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare scheme guidelines and official scheme portals.

schemes.name: PM-KISAN (Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi)
schemes.benefit: Rs 6,000 per year paid directly to the bank account in three equal instalments of Rs 2,000, every four months.
schemes.eligibility: All landholding farmer families with cultivable land in their name. Excludes institutional landholders, income-tax payers, serving/retired government employees above Group D, and professionals such as doctors and lawyers.
schemes.how_to_apply: Register at pmkisan.gov.in or through the nearest Common Service Centre (CSC). Aadhaar, land records and a bank account seeded with Aadhaar are mandatory. e-KYC must be completed to receive instalments.

schemes.name: PMFBY (Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana)
schemes.benefit: Insurance against crop loss from natural calamity, pest attack and disease. Farmer pays a capped premium of 2% of sum insured for kharif crops, 1.5% for rabi crops, and 5% for commercial and horticultural crops; the remainder is subsidised by central and state governments.
schemes.eligibility: All farmers growing notified crops in notified areas, including sharecroppers and tenant farmers. Voluntary for all farmers since 2020.
schemes.how_to_apply: Apply through pmfby.gov.in, a bank branch, a CSC, or an authorised insurance intermediary. Enrolment must be completed before the cut-off date for the season, typically 31 July for kharif and 31 December for rabi.

schemes.name: Kisan Credit Card (KCC)
schemes.benefit: Short-term crop loan up to Rs 3 lakh at 7% interest. Prompt repayment earns a 3% subvention, bringing the effective rate to 4%. Also covers post-harvest expenses, allied activities such as dairy and fisheries, and carries accident insurance cover.
schemes.eligibility: All farmers - owner cultivators, tenant farmers, oral lessees, sharecroppers, and Self Help Group or Joint Liability Group members.
schemes.how_to_apply: Apply at any commercial bank, regional rural bank or co-operative bank, or online through the bank's portal. Requires identity proof, address proof and land documents. Loans up to Rs 1.6 lakh are collateral-free.

schemes.name: Soil Health Card Scheme
schemes.benefit: Free soil testing report covering 12 parameters including N, P, K, pH, organic carbon, sulphur and micronutrients, along with crop-wise fertiliser recommendations. Issued once every two years per landholding.
schemes.how_to_apply: Contact the district or block agriculture office, or a Krishi Vigyan Kendra, to have soil samples collected. Reports can be downloaded from soilhealth.dac.gov.in.

schemes.name: PMKSY - Per Drop More Crop (Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana)
schemes.benefit: Subsidy on micro-irrigation systems - drip and sprinkler. Small and marginal farmers receive 55% of system cost; other farmers receive 45%. Many states top this up further.
schemes.eligibility: All farmers with a assured water source. Priority to small, marginal, SC and ST farmers, and to water-stressed blocks.
schemes.how_to_apply: Apply through the state agriculture or horticulture department, or the PMKSY portal. Requires land records, a water source certificate and a bank account.

schemes.name: PM-KUSUM (Kisan Urja Suraksha evam Utthaan Mahabhiyan)
schemes.benefit: Subsidy for standalone solar agricultural pumps and for solarising existing grid-connected pumps. Central and state subsidy together typically covers about 60% of cost, with 30% available as loan, so the farmer contributes roughly 10%. Surplus power can be sold to the grid.
schemes.eligibility: Individual farmers, groups of farmers, FPOs, panchayats and water user associations.
schemes.how_to_apply: Apply through the state nodal agency listed on the PM-KUSUM portal or the state renewable energy development agency.

schemes.name: e-NAM (National Agriculture Market)
schemes.benefit: Online trading platform linking over 1,000 mandis nationwide, letting farmers discover prices across markets and sell beyond their local mandi. Includes assaying facilities and direct online payment.
schemes.eligibility: All farmers, traders and FPOs. Registration is free.
schemes.how_to_apply: Register at enam.gov.in or at the e-NAM counter of a participating APMC mandi, using Aadhaar and bank details.

schemes.name: MSP (Minimum Support Price) and Procurement
schemes.benefit: Government-announced floor price for 22 mandated crops, plus fair and remunerative price for sugarcane. Procurement at MSP is carried out by FCI, NAFED and state agencies. Under PM-AASHA, price deficiency payment and procurement schemes cover pulses and oilseeds.
schemes.eligibility: Farmers selling notified crops at designated procurement centres, subject to prescribed quality (Fair Average Quality) norms.
schemes.how_to_apply: Register on the state procurement portal before the season, then bring produce to a designated procurement centre with land records and a bank account.

schemes.name: MIDH (Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture)
schemes.benefit: Assistance for establishing orchards and plantations, protected cultivation such as polyhouses and shade nets, post-harvest infrastructure including cold storage and pack houses, and nursery development. Typically 40-50% of cost, higher in hilly and scheduled areas.
schemes.eligibility: Farmers, FPOs, co-operatives and entrepreneurs taking up horticulture activities.
schemes.how_to_apply: Apply to the state horticulture mission or district horticulture officer with a project proposal, land records and bank details.

schemes.name: Formation and Promotion of 10,000 FPOs
schemes.benefit: Financial support of up to Rs 18 lakh per FPO over three years, a matching equity grant of up to Rs 2,000 per farmer member capped at Rs 15 lakh, and a credit guarantee facility up to Rs 2 crore. Enables collective input purchase and bulk marketing.
schemes.eligibility: Groups of farmers, minimum 300 members in plains and 100 in hilly and north-eastern regions.
schemes.how_to_apply: Approach an implementing agency such as SFAC, NABARD or NCDC, or the state agriculture department.

schemes.name: Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF)
schemes.benefit: Rs 1 lakh crore financing facility for post-harvest infrastructure - warehouses, cold chains, grading and sorting units, primary processing. Offers 3% interest subvention on loans up to Rs 2 crore for up to seven years, plus credit guarantee.
schemes.eligibility: Farmers, FPOs, PACS, agri-entrepreneurs, startups, co-operatives and state agencies.
schemes.how_to_apply: Apply on agriinfra.dac.gov.in and select a participating lending institution.

schemes.name: National Mission on Natural Farming (NMNF)
schemes.benefit: Support for chemical-free farming based on cow-derived inputs and on-farm biomass. Assistance of about Rs 15,000 per hectare over three years, plus support for bio-input resource centres, farmer training and certification.
schemes.eligibility: Farmers willing to adopt natural farming practices, preferably in clusters along river corridors and in identified districts.
schemes.how_to_apply: Enrol through the state agriculture department or a Krishi Vigyan Kendra; cluster-based enrolment is preferred.
